CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND  JUDGE FOR CBI CASES, AT BENGALURU (CCH-48) IN  SPL.C.C.NO.455/2015 REGISTERED BY THE MALLESHWARAM  P.S., BENGALURU FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S/ 406 AND 420,
 120B R/W 34 OF IPC AND SEC. 9 OF KARNATAKA PROTECTION  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:10656  CRL.RP No. 284 of 2024 OF INTEREST DEPOSITORS IN FINANCIAL ESTABLISHMENT ACT, 2004 AND DISCHARGE THE PETITIONER FROM THE CHARGES LEVELED AGAINST HIM.

THIS CRL.RP COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Petitioner, who happens to be Accused No.17 in Spl.C.C. No. 455/2015 is invoking the Revisional Jurisdiction of this Court u/Ss 397 & 401 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for assailing the order dated 06.01.2024 whereby his Application filed u/S 227 of the Code, seeking discharge from the criminal case, has been negatived by the learned XLVII Addl. City Civil And Sessions Judge and Judge for CBI Cases, at Bengaluru (CCH-48).
2. Learned Sr. Advocate appearing for the Petitioner vehemently argues that his client was neither a director nor a member of the Cooperative Bank concerned; he had nothing to do with its affairs &
business; the entire case is sought to be made out against him on the basis of fabricated documents;
there is absolutely no case to NC: 2024:KHC:10656 proceed against the Petitioner and the material on record does not prima facie vouch case of the prosecution.
All these aspects having not been duly considered by the Court below, there is abuse of process of the Court/law and therefore, Petition needs to be allowed, argues the counsel.
3. Learned Addl.
SPP appearing for the Respondent - State vehemently opposes the Petition making submission in justification of the impugned order and the reasons it has been constructed.

He contends that at the stage of Section 227 of the Code, what the trial Court has to do is, not holding of a mini trial but considering the prima facie involvement of the accused in the commission of the crime; if there is sufficient ground for proceeding against him, dismissal of Discharge Application is perfectly justified.
So contending, he seeks dismissal of the Petition.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition papers, this Court declines NC: 2024:KHC:10656 indulgence in the matter broadly agreeing with the submission of learned Addl. SPP appearing for the State.
Section 227 r/w Section 228 of the Code is a precious safeguard, as a pre-battle protection conferred upon by the accused by the Parliament.
It is a settled law that the Charge Sheet constitutes prima facie evidentiary material to vouch the commission of offence and therefore, for proceeding further in the matter.

At the stage of Section 227, what the N Shivaprasad vs The State Of Karnataka By on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169752277/
2 Court has to look into is, allegations made in the Charge Sheet and whether the same constitute the offence alleged.

sentences.text: 5. For the purpose of determining whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding against an accused the court possesses a comparatively wider discretion in the exercise of which a conviction can be said reasonably to be possible.
Only prima facie case is to be seen, whether case is beyond reasonable doubt is not to be seen at this stage.

If the court comes to the conclusion that the commission of offence is a probable consequence, a case for framing charge exists, at the stage of framing charge, NC: 2024:KHC:10656 probative value of materials on record cannot be gone into,
vide STATE OF MAHARASHTRA vs. SOMANATH THAPA, AIR 1996 SC 1744.
6.

entities.text: STATE OF MAHARASHTRA vs. SOMANATH THAPA, AIR 1996 SC 1744
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been held by Supreme Court that at the stage of consideration of an application for discharge, the court has to proceed with an assumption that the materials brought on record by the prosecution are true and evaluate the materials to find out whether the facts taken at their face value disclose the existence of the ingredients constituting the offence.
At this stage, only the probative value of the materials has to be gone into and the court is not expected to go deep into the matter to hold a min-trial.

7. The ground vehemently urged by Mr. Nanaiah that the Petitioner is neither a member nor a director of the Cooperative Bank and therefore, his request for discharge ought to have been favorued, is bit difficult to countenance.
The said question obviously is, a question of fact and therefore, can be adjudged only after the trial, NC: 2024:KHC:10656 there being prima facie material on record to assume contra fact position.
Learned judge of the Court below has given cogent reason as to there being a triable case against the Petitioner.
Merely because another view is arguably possible, is no ground for interference in Revisional Jurisdiction which has conventional limitations.
In the above circumstances, the Petition being devoid of merits is liable to be rejected and accordingly it is.

The observations hereinabove made being confined to disposal of the Petition, do not cast their light or shadow on the proceedings of the Court below and that, all contentions of the parties are kept open.
